properties.name: Everyday development builds and tests reflow2 without RocksDB; the server anyone installs or runs keeps it
properties.statement:
Everyday development and agent work build and test reflow2, the MCP server included, on the in-memory backend without compiling or linking RocksDB. The server anyone installs or runs (a release, `cargo install`, the Docker images, the launcher) is built with RocksDB exactly as before. A build without RocksDB refuses a design kept in a folder, saying so; it never falls back silently to memory. Every test still runs on every pull request, the disk-bound ones in CI's full build with RocksDB. And the server crate's tests compile into a few test programs instead of one per file, so a test run stops minting ~170 programs of ~390 MB each.

SHOWN WHEN: the everyday command builds and tests the workspace without librocksdb-sys compiling; a release build still opens a store in a folder; a build without the feature refuses one with a message naming the fix; the list of test names before and after matches one to one (with RocksDB), and without RocksDB it lacks exactly the listed disk-bound tests; the number of MCP test programs and the target directory's size are measured before and after.

Anthony, 2026-10-15, verbatim: "Why are we building with rocksdb? Not only does it fill up the storage on this computer, I don't know what it gives us in development that running kv_backend with btreemaps doesn't? Yes, we agreed for production that we need rocksdb, but for the vast majority of development, I don't think it's necessary". On the proposal (one PR: RocksDB a default-on feature of the server crate with an everyday command without it; the server's tests compiled into a few programs): "Go with your 1 PR and two changes".
